name: Client intake sheet
description: A client's rambling email or call notes, pulled into the same fields in the same order every time.
author: Whisper Unchained
prompt:
Pull the details out of the text (a client's email, a message, or notes from a call) and lay them out as an intake sheet, always in this order.

For each person mentioned as a client, one block:

Name:
Phone:
Email:
Address:
Date of birth:

Then, once:

What they are asking for:
Property or item details:
Dates and deadlines:
Other details:
Not stated:

Rules:
- Copy names, numbers, addresses and dates exactly as written. Do not correct or reformat them, except to put a phone number in one consistent form.
- If a field was not given, write "unknown". If it was given but unclear, write what was said followed by "(unsure)".
- Under "Not stated", list the fields you had to mark unknown, so they can be asked for.
- Never guess or fill in anything that is not in the text. Leave out pleasantries and anything that is not a fact or a request.
- Plain text, one field per line. No commentary before or after.

This is a starting point: edit this instruction so the fields and their order match the form you actually fill in.

Example:
Hi, this is Dana Whitfield, 555 0142. My husband Rob and I want to list our house at 18 Marsh Lane, hoping to be on the market by June 1st
becomes:
Name: Dana Whitfield
Phone: 555-0142
Email: unknown
Address: 18 Marsh Lane
Date of birth: unknown

Name: Rob Whitfield (unsure)
Phone: unknown
Email: unknown
Address: 18 Marsh Lane
Date of birth: unknown

What they are asking for: To list their house for sale
Property or item details: House at 18 Marsh Lane
Dates and deadlines: On the market by June 1st
Other details: Dana and Rob are married
Not stated: Dana's email and date of birth; Rob's phone, email and date of birth
